name: Sequenzy for WooCommerce
author: Sequenzy Team

sections.description:
Sequenzy for WooCommerce connects WordPress sites running WooCommerce to Sequenzy so you can use product, customer, order, cart, and checkout activity in ecommerce email automations.

This extension is specifically for WooCommerce stores. If you only need regular WordPress user sync and comment opt-in subscribers without WooCommerce store data, use the separate Sequenzy Email Marketing plugin.

The extension uses a guided connection flow. A store manager starts the connection from WooCommerce -> Sequenzy, signs in to Sequenzy, and chooses the company that should own the store. No WooCommerce REST API keys are copied into Sequenzy.

Features:

  • Guided Sequenzy connection and reconnection flow.
  • Installation heartbeat so Sequenzy can show connection health.
  • Initial sync for products, customers, and guest buyers.
  • Product created, updated, and deleted event delivery.
  • Customer created and profile-updated event delivery.
  • Order created, completed, cancelled, and refunded event delivery.
  • Cart-started, cart-updated, cart-cleared, and checkout-started event delivery.
  • Retry handling for transient Sequenzy API failures.
  • Recent failure diagnostics in WordPress admin.
  • Disconnect support that clears local connection state.

Third-party service

This extension connects to Sequenzy, a SaaS email marketing and automation platform, after a store manager starts and completes the connection flow.

When connected, the extension sends selected store metadata, product data, customer email addresses and names, order billing details, order totals, cart line items, checkout email addresses, event names, timestamps, plugin version, WordPress version, WooCommerce version, and store URL to the Sequenzy API at https://api.sequenzy.com.

Sequenzy terms: https://sequenzy.com/terms
Sequenzy privacy policy: https://sequenzy.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. In WordPress, go to Plugins -> Add Plugin, search for Sequenzy for WooCommerce, and install it.
  3. Activate Sequenzy for WooCommerce.
  4. Open WooCommerce -> Sequenzy.
  5. Click Connect to Sequenzy.
  6. Sign in to Sequenzy and choose the company that should own the store.
  7. Return to WordPress and click Complete connection.
sections.faq:
Do I need WooCommerce?

Yes. WooCommerce must be installed and active before this extension can sync store data.

Is this the same as Sequenzy Email Marketing?

No. Sequenzy Email Marketing is for regular WordPress subscriber sources such as registered users and comment opt-ins. Sequenzy for WooCommerce is specifically for WooCommerce products, customers, orders, carts, checkout activity, and ecommerce automation events.

Do I need a Sequenzy account?

Yes. You need a Sequenzy account and company workspace to connect the extension.

Does the extension send data before I connect it?

No. The extension only sends data after a store manager completes the Sequenzy connection flow.

Does this create WooCommerce REST API keys?

No. The extension uses a Sequenzy-issued installation token instead of asking you to create WooCommerce REST API keys.

Does this add public links, badges, or storefront output?

No. The extension does not add public credits, badges, or storefront marketing output.

How do I disconnect the store?

Open WooCommerce -> Sequenzy and click Disconnect. The extension clears local connection credentials and asks Sequenzy to revoke the installation.
sections.changelog:
1.0.2

  • Process initial product and customer sync batches reliably in the background and report the real sync outcome instead of always showing a completed sync.
  • Wait out Sequenzy rate limits and retry the affected batch, so syncing a large catalog no longer stops part way through.

1.0.1

  • Send a refreshed full-cart snapshot after every add, removal, and quantity change so cart-abandonment timing and contents stay accurate.

1.0.0

  • Initial WordPress.org release with pairing, product sync, customer sync, order events, cart events, checkout events, retries, and diagnostics.
